transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called us together for the standard production sign-off on the dance special draft. Before I can approve the final stage plan, I need to walk through it with all of you — technical, location, and movement staff. Let's start by going through the current draft elements: the rotating platform, the overhead lift, the floor anchors drilled into the stage, and the two-meter camera lane. I want to hear any concerns or issues from each of your areas before I make my decision.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue before we go further. During a camera-rail test I conducted, I confirmed that the rotating platform would enter the rail's required three-meter exclusion lane. The technically approved layout is actually a fixed platform with a three-meter camera lane. I recorded the test results in the technical log, but I have not yet updated Mara's design draft to reflect this. So the draft you're looking at still shows a rotating platform and a two-meter camera lane, which conflicts with what passed technical review.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical location issue. I confirmed with the Atrium Theater's preservation officer this morning that drilling into the theater floor is prohibited. I received the written restriction today, but it hasn't been added to the location packet yet. The approved replacement requires exactly 18 ballast bases for a freestanding platform. So the floor anchors called for in the current draft cannot be installed as written.
transcript.speaker: A3
